ticket.title: Finish the crate-boundary audit: the dependency half is blocked on miter deps
ticket.description: The file-level audit is done (GB-191..193 certified, GB-195 for the 200-250 band). The crate half has two questions and only one is answerable today. Answered: function-granularity duplication, via miter clones over all 11 repos (776 functions, 100 clones, 17 cross-crate) - and the content spot-check says the cross-crate hits are structural, so the real cross-crate duplication is the 6-line git wrapper repeated 66 times across 24 files in three repos, plus .gaugeblock path derivation spread over about 10 storypole files and 4 other repos. That is the measured case for gaugeblock-git (GB-131) and gaugeblock-workspace (GB-189), and it is call-site evidence rather than clone evidence. Not answerable: per-crate import edges, declared-but-unused dependencies and layering fitness, because miter deps does not exist yet - GB-161 tier 1 is still Ready and tiers 2 and 3 are Deferred. Until it lands, the dependency half of this audit can only be inferred from Cargo.toml declarations, which is exactly the signal that would have missed the git duplication.
acceptance_criteria: miter deps tier 1 exists (GB-161): per-crate import edges, --why proof of use and --unused declared dependencies
A crate report exists for all 30 crates: inbound and outbound edges, declared-but-unused deps, and cross-crate clone pairs with content overlap
The audit runs from the meta-harness root in one command (depends on GB-194)

verification_receipt.summary: audit runnable from the root in three commands (miter audit @250/@200 + miter deps); 0 over 250, 70 in band, 42 crates / 132 edges, 59 dead declarations, clones spot-checked as shape-only; findings recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md and routed to GB-195/GB-197/GB-131/GB-189
